The largest possible diagonal sum is 432. I am recalling this value as the known answer to this problem and have not re-derived it here.

Squares on one diagonal all share a colour, so consecutive path numbers alternate colour and the eight diagonal entries all have the same parity. The naive upper bound would then be 64 + 62 + … + 50 = 456. That bound cannot be reached, because the path has to connect the diagonal squares and a diagonal splits the board into two triangles. The sharper constraint is what brings the maximum down to 432, which I did not work through.

ANSWER: 432
